Strength is graded: strongest (up to max) when the opener is a maximum/minimum-degree marker (superlatives the/-est/best/worst/most including a-most, least, cross-lingual plus/mas forms, and comparatives more/-er...than), peaking on the phrase's head noun or its closing qualifier (in/of/on/ever/never) or the following subject pronoun (I/they/he); moderate on fronted subordinate or adverbial frames (while/when/since/if/after/before), quoted dialogue attribution, fronted wh-frames (Whoever/Which...), bare ever/never continuations, and code lines (strongest on declarations such as #define/private, variable on expression statements); superlatives embedded in adjunct PPs (with the best...) or bare recipe imperatives (Use the deepest pan...) are variable and can read below the line, and reliably below the line are only short single-clause fragments with no such opener and plain lists of bare numbers.
